LifeBridge

Connecting Crisis to Care

An AR/VR-based emergency-response prototype designed to reduce delayed help after accidents through quick first-aid guidance and immersive emergency training.

Open Working Prototype ↗View Screenshots

Patna Women's College · Team Infinity

Problem Statement

Delayed professional help and lack of immediate first-aid knowledge can make the first few minutes after an accident critical.

Road accidents often require immediate first aid, but professional medical help may take time to arrive. People present at the accident site may not know the correct emergency steps, which can lead to delayed or improper assistance. LifeBridge aims to reduce this gap using AR-based real-time guidance and VR-based emergency-response training.
AR

Real-time Guidance

Quick on-screen emergency instructions during a real accident situation.

VR

Safe Training

A simulated environment where users can practice emergency-response steps.

Goal

Faster Response

Use the critical waiting time effectively until professional care arrives.

Prototype Overview

LifeBridge is a student prototype intended to support emergency response, not replace professional medical care.

AR

Emergency Guidance

Provides quick guidance such as checking scene safety, checking the victim, calling emergency help, controlling bleeding, and showing CPR-related instructions.

VR

Emergency Training

Allows the learner to practice scene assessment, victim interaction, calling for help, breathing checks, and CPR-related response in a virtual environment.
